--- title: "[Graph.random_walk_with_restart()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Random walk with restart (RWR) from a set of seed nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24321-L24473){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.random_walk_with_restart( seeds, restart_prob=0.15, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random walk with restart](/assets/graphs/random-walk-with-restart.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same seven-node two-cluster graph with the seed A (node id 1) outlined and every node shaded by its steady-state visit probability for a walker that jumps back to A with probability 0.15 at each step. The table reads A 0.27, B and C 0.22, D 0.14, E 0.07, and F and G 0.03." width="100%"} At each step the walker either follows a random outgoing edge (with probability `1 - restart_prob`) or teleports back to one of the seed nodes (with probability `restart_prob`). Returns the steady-state visitation probability for every node. RWR is mathematically equivalent to Personalized PageRank. This method provides a more intuitive interface for the common genomics use case of propagating scores from GWAS hits through a protein-protein interaction network. When the walker restarts, it picks a seed in proportion to its value in `seeds=`, and a walker stuck on a node with no outgoing edges also returns to the seeds. Nodes that are close to the seeds, or reachable from them along many short paths, end up with the highest scores. Typical uses: - prioritizing candidate disease genes by their network proximity to known or GWAS-associated genes - spreading a signal from a few labelled nodes to the rest of the network - measuring how strongly every node is associated with a chosen set of nodes In directed graphs the walker only moves along edge direction; in undirected graphs it can move either way. Edge weights are not used: every outgoing edge is equally likely. The scores are written to the node DataFrame every time, including when `return_dict=True`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [seeds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping seed node IDs to initial scores (e.g., ``-log10(p_value)`` from GWAS). Values are normalized internally, so only their relative sizes matter. Nodes not in the dictionary are never restart targets, and IDs that are not in the graph are ignored. [restart_prob]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.15]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Probability of teleporting back to a seed node at each step. Higher values keep the walk closer to the seeds. Typical range: `0.1`-`0.3`. The default is `0.15`, which corresponds to the usual PageRank damping of `0.85`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations. The default is `100`, which is enough for typical `restart_prob=` values; very small `restart_prob=` values converge more slowly and may need more. If the limit is reached, the current scores are returned without warning. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance. Iteration stops once the summed absolute change in all scores between two steps falls below this value. The default is `1e-6`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name for the node DataFrame. Defaults to `"rwr"`. An existing column with this name is overwritten. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns the score dictionary (the scores are still stored under `attr_name=`). If `False` (default), stores the scores in the node DataFrame and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: steady-state visitation probabilities for all nodes, as a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores that sum to `1.0`. Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `seeds=` is empty or its values do not sum to a positive number. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~personalized_pagerank`) : The same computation, parameterized by `damping=`. [](`~network_smooth`) : Smooth existing scores over the network instead. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this four-gene ring the walker restarts at `BRCA1`, which therefore scores highest. Its two direct neighbors, `TP53` and `CHEK2`, tie, and `ATM`, two steps away on the opposite side, scores lowest: ::: {#f2a8ae5b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["BRCA1", "TP53", "ATM", "CHEK2"]) .add_edges([("BRCA1", "TP53"), ("TP53", "ATM"), ("ATM", "CHEK2"), ("BRCA1", "CHEK2")]) ) seed_id = graph.get_id_from_label("BRCA1") scores = graph.random_walk_with_restart( seeds={seed_id: 1.0}, restart_prob=0.15, return_dict=True, ) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 4) for nid, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'ATM': 0.1953, 'BRCA1': 0.3453, 'CHEK2': 0.2297, 'TP53': 0.2297} ``` ::: ::: A higher `restart_prob=` keeps the walker near the seed, so `BRCA1` gets more of the total and `ATM` much less: ::: {#c23aad68 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} scores = graph.random_walk_with_restart( seeds={seed_id: 1.0}, restart_prob=0.5, return_dict=True, ) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 4) for nid, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'ATM': 0.0833, 'BRCA1': 0.5833, 'CHEK2': 0.1667, 'TP53': 0.1667} ``` ::: ::: Seeds can carry GWAS evidence directly. Here `BRCA1` (p = 1e-8) gets twice the weight of `ATM` (p = 1e-4), and with `attr_name=` the scores are stored as a node column. Both seeds now score above the non-seed genes: ::: {#927bfea6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import math seeds = { graph.get_id_from_label("BRCA1"): -math.log10(1e-8), graph.get_id_from_label("ATM"): -math.log10(1e-4), } graph.random_walk_with_restart(seeds, attr_name="rwr_gwas") graph.get_node_df().select(["label", "rwr_gwas"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
